The build passes. Here's a summary of what I changed.

## Summary

The new acceptance test asserts that a rejected `POST /api/owners` returns an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with a `status` member matching the HTTP status. Two small, cohesive edits made this work while keeping structural impact low:

1. **`OwnerPostcodeValidationAdvice.validate`** — the missing-`city` rejection case was actually crashing with a 500 `NullPointerException` before the 400 could ever be produced: `Map.of(...).get(owner.getCity())` throws when the city is `null` (an immutable map rejects a null key). I made the region lookup null-safe:
   ```java
   String city = owner.getCity();
   int[] range = city == null ? null : CITY_RANGE.get(city);
   ```
   With the crash gone, validation proceeds normally and the blank-`city` rejection surfaces as a proper `400` — which `ExceptionControllerAdvice` already renders as a `ProblemDetail` (`application/problem+json`, with `type`/`title`/`status`/`detail`).

2. **`ResponseStatusExceptionAdvice.handleResponseStatusException`** — the `409`/`429` rejections thrown as `ResponseStatusException` previously returned an empty `ResponseEntity<Void>`. I changed it to return a `ProblemDetail` carrying the same status, so those rejections now also emit an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail` — HTTP status codes unchanged.

Both edits are confined to two tiny classes (each with near-zero surrounding complexity), avoiding any change to the large `ExceptionControllerAdvice`. Full suite: `BUILD SUCCESS`, all tests green.
